renderer_provenance.scope: Only plot labels/dimensions, an installed-capacity title and a canonical SLO reference line changed after the simulation source was committed. Model, admission, execution, audit, aggregation, inputs and numerical results are unchanged. Figures are rendered again with the updated plot function.

replay_schedule_sensitivity_example.scope: Saved-wave arithmetic; near-identical aggregate admitted masses can have different feedback admission schedules. This is not evidence that more WAN makes physical replay slower.

replay_selection_exception.scope: Saved pack allocations differ between the lowest cap and all higher caps. Every admitted wave completes before 30 s in both cases; the handoff difference is selected/admitted work, not an admitted replay missing its deadline. Refinement iterations and small nonzero log timings also differ; this diagnostic does not identify a unique optimizer cause.

saved_case_runtime_s.scope: Sum of recorded per-case simulate_s and audit_s; excludes candidate construction, initial setup, final plotting and this independent review. It is not a separate wall-clock campaign duration.

scope: Read-only verification of saved policy outputs; no policy optimization, GPU measurement or full request replay was rerun for this grid audit.

Candidate identifiers are compared across every record; full candidate arrays are not re-generated in this review. Fleet metadata, timing-report hashes and resident templates are independently rebuilt from the frozen code and measurements.

Resident windows select original offers and preserve unfinished service. All 2 × 6666 destination GPUs contribute, including unused resident-only replicas; source-site service is outside this destination denominator.

Global weighted resident attainment and strict per-wave/two-seed local targets are separate. Each 30 s window is tested before selecting a worst-window global value, so later successful arrivals cannot dilute an early window.

Five replay-only workload/deadline blocks preserve aggregate handoff within 1e-7. Long D30 at 0.1 Tbps differs by 0.0392554461 percentage points from every higher cap: admitted pack allocation/refinement changes, while every admitted wave completes before the deadline. Nonzero log transfer time and nearly tied admission schedules may also change phase timing, threshold crossings and conditional resident metrics; outcomes are preserved rather than forced invariant.

Scalar execution checks enforce recorded network/compute budgets, source history conservation, action masks and fluid resident-debt conservation. They do not reconstruct every intermediate physical network rate or re-solve the LP.

Post-plan request checks condition on frozen network releases, source snapshots and handoff gates. Timing-incompatible or locally passing subsets are descriptive subsets of one fixed plan; removing waves would require rescheduling.

Warm idle initial prefixes, two synthesized phase seeds, no prefix eviction, one incoming pack per GPU, constant decode cadence transferred across regions and fixed 80 Gb/s host reservations remain explicit model assumptions.

Source turn durations use incremental-prefill warm-context costs even at resets/cycle wraps and do not serialize GPU service across source histories; this remains an optimistic source-service floor. Destination request templates explicitly clear same-history cached prefixes at those reset/wrap boundaries.
Neither this audit nor previously failed measured resident gates certify fleet SLOs or actual net datacenter power shed.
